identity.title: MLKL-dependent necroptosis contributes to FB1-induced lung injury in swine.

content.abstract: Pulmonary edema is a hallmark of fumonisin B1 (FB1) poisoning in pigs, characterized by pulmonary hemorrhage and fluid accumulation. Necroptosis is a regulated form of cell death that compromises plasma membrane integrity, leading to the release of cytoplasmic contents. This study aimed to investigate whether necroptosis is involved in FB1-induced disruption of vascular endothelial barrier integrity and subsequent pulmonary edema. Preliminary experiments showed that FB1 could induce lung injury and necroptosis in pigs. The underlying mechanisms were further investigated in vitro. The results suggested that FB1 triggers necroptosis and impairs barrier integrity in porcine lung microvascular endothelial cells. CRISPR Cas9-mediated knockout of mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) alleviated this barrier disruption. Furthermore, in Mlkl(-/-) mice, enhanced resistance to FB1-induced pulmonary hemorrhage, edema, and barrier damage was observed compared to wild-type mice, suggesting that MLKL deficiency plays a critical role in mitigating FB1-triggered pulmonary edema. In conclusion, MLKL-dependent necroptotic pathway is involved in FB1-induced disruption of vascular endothelial barrier integrity, thereby inducing porcine pulmonary edema. Targeting MLKL is a promising strategy to prevent its development.
